Looking at how `initializeMcpState` is called in handlers/agent.ts and whether errors are properly caught, plus checking `_ensureGitignore`. The core problem seems to be that `_initialize` calls `_ensureSpecs`, which tries to create directories, and if the project folder is read-only or mounted as read-only in Docker with non-root permissions, the mkdir fails and that error bubbles up uncaught.

Since `_initPromise` is awaited in the agent handler, this initialization failure causes the entire chat request to fail, even for simple database queries that shouldn't need those specs at all. Let me check the agent handler to see how this promise is being awaited.

I've confirmed the mechanism, so now I'm investigating why this issue appeared specifically after upgrading to 0.3.0 — it seems the on-disk spec writing architecture might be new to that version, whereas earlier versions loaded MCP tools directly into context. I need to check the git history and version records to see when this disk-writing behavior was introduced, and also look at how the user's environment is configured with non-root permissions and read-only mounts.

content.text: So `_writeEnabledSpecs` was introduced in a recent feature commit and hasn't been released yet—it'll ship in version 0.3.0, which aligns with when the upgrade happened. Now I need to look at the Dockerfile to check the user configuration and the /app/project directory.

I'm looking at the deployment path `/app/project` where users mount their project, likely with different ownership than the `nao` user (UID 1000). The Dockerfile sets up `/app/context` and `/app/projects` owned by nao, but a bind-mounted `/app/project` will inherit the host's ownership. I should verify this mount path in the entrypoint script and documentation, and check whether there are any notes about read-only mounting.

So the issue is that files copied into the Docker image during the build are owned by root, but the backend process runs as the `nao` user via supervisord, which means it can't create directories under `/app/project/agent/mcps` due to permission errors. I should look at the supervisord configuration to understand how the process is being run.

The MCP initialization is unconditional and attempts to create directories for each configured server (like `airtable`), and since `_initPromise` gets reset to null on failure, every chat request retries and fails at the same point before the agent even gets created. Let me verify the supervisord user configuration.
